newsitem.title: UK: Eurotunnel gets mixed decision in TML claim.
newsitem.headline: Eurotunnel gets mixed decision in TML claim.

text.p: Anglo-French Channel Tunnel operator Eurotunnel said on Tuesday it received a mixed decision in its dispute with construction consortium TML over rolling stock.

Eurotunnel said the Panel of Experts, which addresses disputes between the firm and TML, decided that the company was entitled to damages for deficiencies in some rolling stock but rejected Eurotunnel's demands relating to losses in revenue.
In addition, the Panel declared a counterclaim by TML inadmissible, Eurotunnel said.
Regarding damages for the rolling stock, the panel encouraged the parties to negotiate between themselves on the appropriate compensation, the company said.

"While recognising the merits of the majority of Eurotunnel's claims, the Panel declared a large number inadmissible on the basis of contractual principles which it judged applicable," Eurotunnel said in a statement.
The company said its board would decide during one of its meetings what follow-up action it would take and whether it would submit the case for arbitration by the International Chamber of Commerce.
The Panel's decision may be submitted within the next 90 days for ICC arbitration.
Eurotunnel's claim was submitted to the Panel in December 1995 and alleged inadequacies in rolling stock supplied by TML.
Eurotunnel's shares were up a penny at 71.5 in London by 0800 GMT.
Eurotunnel made headlines late last year when a fire damaged one of its main tunnels and some rolling stock.
An internal inquiry by the company later cleared its systems and equipment of any blame for causing the fire. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
